Applications for open LIHEAP 2026-27 program 
 WJET/WFXP/YourErie.com 
 Applications for open LIHEAP 2026-27 program
 Drew Miller 
 2 hours ago 
 (WJET/WFXP)– The Pennsylvania Department of Human Services (PA DHS) announced that applications have opened applications for LIHEAP grants worth up to $1,000 to help Pennsylvanians keep their homes warm this upcoming winter. 
 Applications opened this week for the program that helps hundreds of thousands of households across the Commonwealth, giving out cash and crisis grants worth up to $1,000 each season. 
 Flights from Erie to Las Vegas starting in January 
 Each year, LIHEAP pays those funds directly to utility providers for eligible households that are in danger of having their heating utility turned off, have already had it turned off or are out of or have less than two weeks’ worth of deliverable fuel. 
 Individuals and families are financially eligible for LIHEAP if their incomes are at or below 150 percent of the Federal Poverty Limit. For an individual, that is a gross income of $23,940 per year, and for a family of four, that is a gross income of $49,500 per year for the 2026-2027 LIHEAP season.
 Last year, PA DHS said 278,910 households received $289 on average in cash grants and 121,329 households received $599 on average in crisis benefits, with officials encouraging anyone who received benefits last year to apply again. 
 Poplar St. post office re-opening delayed to December 
 “Pennsylvanians need to be able to heat their homes and keep themselves and their families warm through the winter, and LIHEAP helps hundreds of thousands of Pennsylvanians each year stay safe and healthy during the coldest months of the year,” said PA DHS Secretary Dr. Val Arkoosh. “Anyone who may need help with heating costs and keeping their home safe through this winter should apply for LIHEAP as soon as possible.”
 In addition to LIHEAP benefits, PA DHS said several utility companies offer programs that reduce monthly bills, debt forgiveness and other types of assistance, with more information available on the PA PUC website . You can apply for LIHEAP benefits online here .
